title: Bind Claude model and effort launch selection
description: Objective: make the real Claude launcher prove which provider/model/effort/profile/config selection it actually launches. Deliverable: an exact launch-selection contract and pre-open verifier composed into ClaudeLaunchRequest snapshotting and launchClaude so selectedModelId, dated snapshot/build evidence, reasoning effort, profile revision, configuration/policy/orchestration digests, and concurrency ceiling cannot disagree with argv or be supplied only after the run. Consumer: task-159f4c21ef9149e8a65f24735c9c1475. NOT in scope: parsing provider result usage, benchmark records, daemon dispatch, pricing, or treating runtime version/profileRevisionId as model evidence. Owned paths: focused packages/runner/src/providers/claude selection module/bridge/tests and minimal claude-launcher contract/input/entry wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: ClaudeLaunchRequest snapshot carries an exact frozen launch selection distinct from runtime/profile facts, including provider, selected model ID, explicit snapshot/build evidence or UNKNOWN, reasoning effort, profile revision, configuration/policy/orchestration digests, and a positive concurrency ceiling.

Before runtime preparation, grant consumption, lock acquisition, or boundary open, production launchClaude verifies a unique exact argv model/effort selection against the snapshotted contract; duplicate, missing, alias-only, accessor/proxy, or conflicting evidence refuses with a stable exact TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION code/layer and zero downstream effect.

Runtime reportedVersion/closure and profileRevisionId remain separately bound and can never satisfy model snapshot/build or reasoning-effort fields; dated exact model evidence is preserved while unavailable snapshot evidence is explicit UNKNOWN.
Focused production-path tests assert every selection evidence arm has non-zero exact cardinality, pin code/layer and downstream cutoffs, and mutation-check model and effort comparisons independently.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not infer model or effort solely from caller telemetry, environment defaults, settings aliases, runtime reportedVersion, or profileRevisionId.
Selection validation happens before provider/open authority and never echoes argv secrets in refusals.
Do not grow claude-launcher-lifecycle.ts or claude-launcher-port-results.ts; both are already at the 250-line target.

comments.author: architect-b1a46457
comments.content:
Planning decision on the code/layer name, recorded so QA grades against a written choice rather than its own reading of DoD 2.

MEASURED: `TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION` does not exist anywhere in the repository. `grep -rn "TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git` returns exactly one hit — the DoD sentence inside this task's own JSON. No code ending in `_CONFIGURATION` exists in packages/ or apps/ (positive control on `_UNSUPPORTED` with identical flags hits immediately). The string TELEMETRY appears zero times under packages/runner. The only TELEMETRY_* symbol repo-wide is @moe/contracts' `RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_KINDS = ["presence.ping"]`, a wire-KIND array with no paired layer.

DECIDED SPELLINGS. New LAYER, literally `TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION`, appended to the two inline literals at the end of CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS. Seven new CODES appended to the private LOCAL_CODES array: CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_MALFORMED, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_MODEL_UNPROVEN, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_MODEL_AMBIGUOUS, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_MODEL_MISMATCH, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_EFFORT_UNPROVEN, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_EFFORT_AMBIGUOUS, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_EFFORT_MISMATCH.

THREE REASONS, all measured. (1) DoD 2's phrase is "a stable exact TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION code/layer"; the layer spelling satisfies that literally. (2) Every launcher-local code in the resolved 93-member CLAUDE_LAUNCH_ERROR_CODES carries one of four owned prefixes — CLAUDE_RUNTIME_*, the supervisor family, PROCESS_BOUNDARY_*, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_* — and a bare `TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION` code would match none of them. (3) DoD 4 requires model and effort to be "mutation-check[ed] independently". That is only mechanically possible if they refuse with DIFFERENT codes; a single shared code makes the two drills indistinguishable and the requirement unsatisfiable. Drills D1/D2 in step 9 exist to prove exactly this: breaking the model comparison must redden the model cases while the effort cases stay green, and vice versa.

COST: zero test edits. Neither CLAUDE_LAUNCH_ERROR_CODES (93 members) nor CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LAYERS (17) carries a single length or membership assertion anywhere — all 17 references repo-wide are three `toContain` plus one `Object.isFrozen` in the launcher suite, one `toContain` in index-surface, two export-kind rows, and the production `oneOf()` decoder. Appending to SUPERVISOR_ERROR_CODES instead was rejected: effect-properties.test.ts:248 is a closed-set REACHABILITY sweep, not a length pin, so a new member there must actually be returned by a production supervisor refusal.

TWO OTHER DECISIONS WORTH FLAGGING BEFORE WORK STARTS.

Gate placement: after the duplicate short-circuit, before prepareRuntime. DoD 2 names exactly four things the gate must precede and duplicate resolution is not among them; adoption and EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH open no process and consume no grant, and the adopted process was gated by the launch that created it. Placing it earlier would break the existing `expect(log).toEqual(["duplicate"])` for no safety gain.

The default `request()` fixture gains a valid selection and matching argv. `request()` has dozens of call sites across claude-launcher.test.ts and claude-launcher-authority.test.ts, and eight of the nine pre-open table cases build from it while pinning codes produced by LATER phases — a gate refusing the default would flip all of them at once and every one would then be testing the gate instead of its own subject. Drill D3 proves the gate is not silently answering for them.

Also for whoever picks this up: the runner suite is RED right now from task-de496f47's in-flight tests-first loop, which is not this task's defect and not this task's to repair. Step 1 captures the attribution baseline before any byte is written.

⚠️ FIVE VERIFIED DEFECTS IN `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts` — from Yaron's 2026-08-14 product audit (30-agent sweep with adversarial verification), posted to #general 23:06:38Z. **The human deliberately did NOT fix these because the file is live launcher-task territory and you are the task working in it.** Recording here so they are not lost to chat scroll.

All five are confirmed, not speculative:

1. **Verifier timeout kills only the `cmd.exe` shell; the grandchild test process leaks.** Classic Windows shell-spawn defect — killing the shell orphans what it launched. Same family as the detached-grandchild kill proof already landed in the broker work.

4. **A non-numeric `MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS` silently disables the concurrency cap.** Fails open — the cap vanishes rather than refusing. Directly against epic rail 4 (fail closed with stable reason codes); a bad env value must refuse with a named code, never silently unbound.
5. **A stdin write on a failed spawn is an unhandled stream error on POSIX.**

**Scope judgement is yours and I am not widening your task.** If your current DoD does not reach agent-wrapper-main.ts, do not absorb these — say so and I will route them to a dedicated task rather than let you take an out-of-scope diff into QA. What I want to avoid is you touching that file for the model/effort binding, walking past these, and a later task rediscovering them from scratch.

**Cross-checks worth doing while you are in there,** since 3 and 4 are the cheap ones and their tests are the kind that rot: for 4, assert the *reason code* on the non-numeric value, not merely that the cap was not applied — "returned an error" is one added layer away from vacuous. For 3, a fixture path with a literal space is required; a backslash or space fixture written through a shell or `node -e` collapses before it reaches the assertion, so build it with the file-edit tool, not a shell heredoc.

A single shared code would make the two mutation drills indistinguishable. REJECTED alternatives: minting a bare TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION code (breaks the vocabulary's prefix discipline and makes DoD 4 unsatisfiable), and reusing @moe/contracts' RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_KINDS (a wire-kind array, not a refusal vocabulary, with no layer).

2) GATE PLACEMENT — chosen: AFTER the duplicate short-circuit, BEFORE prepareRuntime (insertion point L129/L130). DoD 2 names exactly four things the gate must precede — runtime preparation, grant consumption, lock acquisition, boundary open — and duplicate resolution is not among them. Adoption and EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH open no process and consume no grant, and the process being adopted was itself gated by the earlier launchClaude that created it, so gating adoption adds no safety. Placing it BEFORE the duplicate branch would additionally break the existing `expect(log).toEqual(["duplicate"])` assertion for no benefit. REJECTED: before the duplicate branch.

3) WHERE THE SELECTION RIDES — chosen: a new `launchSelection` field on ClaudeLaunchRequest, forcing the five-site edit. REJECTED: riding on ClaudeLaunchOptions, which is tempting because snapshotLaunchEntry reads only three named keys and TOLERATES extras, so it costs no key-list edit — but DoD 1 says explicitly "ClaudeLaunchRequest snapshot carries an exact frozen launch selection", and options is not exact-key-closed, which is precisely the wrong property for evidence that must not be forgeable. REJECTED: riding on the openBoundary payload — impossible, windows-launch-request.ts pins a closed 4-key record in production.

4) THE DEFAULT FIXTURE — chosen: `request()` gains a VALID default selection AND a matching argv model/effort pair, so every existing call site keeps passing. REJECTED: passing a selection explicitly at every call site — `request()` is called 39 times in claude-launcher.test.ts and 18 times in claude-launcher-authority.test.ts, and a gate that refuses the default fixture flips all nine pre-open table cases at once plus both suites. The obvious objection to the cheap option — "then no test proves the gate fires on the default path" — is answered by dedicated override cases plus drills D1/D2, not by 57 edits.

5) TASK SIZE — chosen: ONE task at ten distinct files, which is at the hard cap but not over it. REJECTED: splitting contract-plus-snapshot from verifier-plus-gate. The two are separable on paper, but a landed selection contract with no verifier is exactly the "proves only the shapes" artifact the epic rail condemns, and splitting would double the churn on claude-launcher-test-fixtures.ts, claude-launcher.test.ts and index-surface.test.ts — the three most contended files in the repo right now, with three other agents already editing this directory. Governors: this is a deliberate size decision on plan shape, not a LOC exception.

6) EVIDENCE BINDING — REJECTED as out of scope: adding the selection to the launch observation digest. argv is absent from claude-launcher-lifecycle.ts entirely, DoD 2 asks only for pre-open verification, and rail 3 forbids growing that file.

issues.description: CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_FLAGS freezes effort as --reasoning-effort, but `claude --help` and Anthropic's CLI reference specify `--effort`. Production probe: [`--model`, id, `--effort`, `high`] => CLAUDE_LAUNCH_EFFORT_UNPROVEN/TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION; replacing it with `--reasoning-effort` => ok:true. Change to the real provider flag and add a hand-spelled (not production-constant-derived) launchClaude positive test so the provider contract cannot drift green.

The verifier examines launchSelection and argv but not request.environment, while the request environment is forwarded to the provider at lines 204-205. Claude's documented CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL overrides other effort-setting methods, so an environment value `low` can defeat a claimed/argv `high`. Refuse any effective-effort conflict at TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION with the exact stable reason and zero boundary/provider effects; add the production launch regression.

Production probes accepted transparent Proxy launchSelection and argv values; an ownKeys trap executed once and the selection still returned ok:true. A hostile selectedModelId object also caused String(...) coercion to invoke a throwing toString and escape. Reject proxies/hostile descriptors before reflective access or coercion, contain revoked/throwing traps, and assert the exact TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION code/layer on the production surface.

snapshotClaudeLaunchRequest collapses an invalid nested launch selection to null, so launchClaude answers CLAUDE_LAUNCH_REQUEST_MALFORMED/LAUNCHER before the dedicated selection guard; the integration test currently pins this wrong layer. Preserve and return the selection-specific stable refusal at TELEMETRY_CONFIGURATION for missing/duplicate/accessor/proxy/conflict cases, with zero provider/boundary effects.

In addition, launchClaude forwards CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL without validating its higher-precedence override, so claimed/argv high can actually launch low. Fix the real flag and environment precedence, make hostile input total and proxy-closed, preserve the selection guard's exact layer, and add hand-spelled production-bound regressions with zero downstream effects. Foreign concurrent fixture WIP appeared after the green gate and is disclosed but is not attributed to this task.
